newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks retreat as regulators meet.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks retreat as regulators meet.

text.p: Caution ruled Indian share markets on Friday after recent wild gyrations, as regulators held a closed-door meeting with exchange chiefs on excess speculation, traders said.
Optimism that the government was preparing moves to reverse slowing industrial growth and to jump-start markets ignited heavy speculative bidding in blue chip stocks.
But seven straight days of gains that saw a 12 percent rise from the New Year ended on Thursday in frantic, volatile trading.

"We are being extremely vigilant in terms of ensuring that nobody violates the specified turnover limits..," said Ravi Narayan, deputy managing director of the National Stock Exchange (NSE), which operates from 53 centres across India.
The turnover limit is pegged at 33 times a broker's capital adequacy norm, he said.

The Economic Times newspaper on Friday quoted Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) chairman D.R. Mehta as saying the regulator would not interfere with the market movements but would ensure all surveillance and monitoring systems were in order.
"We have found all the exchanges imposed margins and price bands on the upside and also on the downside," Mehta said. "The integrity of the markets have not been disturbed."
On Thursday, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell more than nine percent from its intra-day high in volatile trade.
"By and large the market has been driven by huge trading volumes," said Maulik Sharedalal, a member-broker of the BSE.
SEBI began a meeting with the chiefs of major exchanges on Friday to find ways to rein in excessive speculation.
But brokers said the market watchdog was unlikely to impose a host of new measures to curb volatility.
"We hope to see some tighter margins," said Sharedalal. "The (SEBI) meeting is likely to be a case of precautionary measure."
Narayan said the NSE shut off the trading terminals of 11 members on Thursday when their business exceeded the stipulated turnover limits.
In late afternoon trade, the BSE top 30-share index ended 32.28 points, or 0.93 percent, down at a provisional 3,423.60.
"I think Thursday's sell-off has put the brakes on the buying euphoria," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
